words.definition: vt. 触发，引发；n. 扳机；诱因

examples.en: The report triggered a heated debate over privacy protection.
examples.zh: 该报告引发了一场关于隐私保护的热烈争论。

examples.en: A spike in food prices could trigger social unrest in the region.
examples.zh: 食品价格飙升可能引发该地区的社会动荡。

words.usage: trigger a crisis／debate／response 引发危机、辩论、反应；the trigger for sth 某事的诱因；pull the trigger 扣扳机，引申下定决心。
collocations: trigger a debate 引发争论
pull the trigger 扣动扳机
the trigger for sth 某事的诱因
words.mnemonic: 原义扳机→一扣即响→触发；诱因

words.definition: n. 继任者；接替者；继承人

examples.en: The retiring CEO named his successor three months in advance.
examples.zh: 即将退休的首席执行官提前三个月指定了继任者。

examples.en: The new model is widely seen as a worthy successor to the original.
examples.zh: 新型号被普遍视为前代的合格继任者。

words.usage: successor to sb／sth 某人或某物的接替者；appoint／name a successor 指定继任者。派生：succession n. 继任；successive adj. 相继的，三词同源常一起记。
collocations: appoint a successor 任命继任者
successor to the throne 王位继承人
a worthy successor 名副其实的继任者
words.mnemonic: suc(下)+cess(走)+or(人)→跟上来接位的人→继任者

words.definition: adj. 连续的；接连的

examples.en: The region has suffered droughts for three successive years.
examples.zh: 该地区已连续三年遭受旱灾。

examples.en: Successive governments failed to reform the outdated tax system.
examples.zh: 历届政府都未能改革过时的税收制度。

words.usage: 只作定语：successive governments／years 连续几届政府、接连数年；与 successful 拼写易混。派生：successively adv. 接连地；succession n. 连续、继任。
collocations: successive governments 历届政府
for three successive years 连续三年
successive generations 世世代代
words.mnemonic: suc(下)+cess(走)+ive→一茬接一茬走→连续的

words.definition: adj. 有抵抗力的；抗拒的

examples.en: Many bacteria have become resistant to common antibiotics.
examples.zh: 许多细菌已对常用抗生素产生耐药性。

examples.en: Some employees remain resistant to changes in the workflow.
examples.zh: 一些员工对工作流程的调整仍有抵触情绪。

words.usage: be resistant to sth 两义皆高频：细菌耐药（drug-resistant bacteria），人对变革抵触。派生：resistance n. 抵抗；耐药性；resist v. 抵制。
collocations: be resistant to 对…有抵抗力
drug-resistant bacteria 耐药菌
water-resistant material 防水材料
words.mnemonic: re(回)+sist(站)+ant→站回去顶住→抵抗的

words.definition: adj. 及时的；vt. 促使；n. 提示

examples.en: Rising costs prompted the company to relocate its factory overseas.
examples.zh: 成本上涨促使公司将工厂迁往海外。

examples.en: We appreciate your prompt reply to our inquiry.
examples.zh: 感谢贵方对询盘的及时回复。

words.usage: prompt sb to do sth 促使某人做某事；形容词义及时的（a prompt reply）；名词义提示词，AI 语境高频。派生：promptly adv. 立即；promptness n. 敏捷。

confusables.note: 促进，多 o 发音不同

collocations: prompt sb to do 促使某人做
a prompt reply 及时回复
writing prompts 写作提示
words.mnemonic: pro(向前)+mpt(拿)→拿到前面推一把→促使；及时的

words.definition: vt. （明令）禁止；阻止

examples.en: Federal law prohibits discrimination on the basis of race or gender.
examples.zh: 联邦法律禁止基于种族或性别的歧视。

examples.en: High borrowing costs prohibit many young families from buying homes.
examples.zh: 高昂的借贷成本使许多年轻家庭无力购房。

words.usage: prohibit sb from doing sth 正式、法律层面禁止；区别 forbid 日常命令、ban 官方取缔。派生：prohibitive adj. 价格高得负担不起的，熟词僻义。
collocations: prohibit sb from doing 禁止某人做
strictly prohibited 严格禁止
prohibitive prices 高得买不起的价格
words.mnemonic: pro(前)+hibit(拿住)→提前拿住不让动→禁止

words.definition: n. 忠告；律师；vt. 劝告，建议

examples.en: The committee sought counsel from independent experts before voting.
examples.zh: 委员会表决前征求了独立专家的意见。

examples.en: Defense counsel argued that the evidence had been mishandled.
examples.zh: 辩护律师辩称证据保管不当。

words.usage: counsel sb to do 劝告某人做；keep one's own counsel 将想法秘而不宣；the counsel for the defense 辩方律师。派生：counselor n. 顾问。
collocations: legal counsel 法律顾问
keep one's own counsel 不露声色
counsel sb to do sth 劝告某人做某事
words.mnemonic: 同源 council 议事会→聚众商议→忠告；律师

words.definition: vt. 控告；vi. 起诉

examples.en: Consumer groups threatened to sue the manufacturer over faulty airbags.
examples.zh: 消费者团体威胁就缺陷气囊起诉制造商。

examples.en: The star sued the tabloid for libel and won substantial damages.
examples.zh: 那位明星起诉小报诽谤，获得巨额赔偿。

words.usage: sue sb for sth 因某事起诉某人，高频句型；sue for damages 诉请赔偿；常与 settle out of court 庭外和解同现。名词 suit 诉讼：file a suit 提起诉讼。
collocations: sue sb for damages 起诉某人索赔
sue for libel 起诉诽谤
threaten to sue 威胁起诉
words.mnemonic: 谐音「诉」→起诉；sue for… 因…而告

words.definition: n. 胜利；凯旋；vi. 获胜

examples.en: The peace treaty was hailed as a triumph of diplomacy.
examples.zh: 和平条约被誉为外交上的重大胜利。

examples.en: Against all odds, the underdog triumphed in the final.
examples.zh: 出人意料，不被看好的一方在决赛中获胜。

words.usage: triumph over sb／sth 战胜；a triumph of diplomacy 外交的胜利；in triumph 得胜地。派生：triumphant adj. 得胜的。区别 victory 泛指一般胜利。
collocations: triumph over adversity 战胜逆境
a triumph of diplomacy 外交的胜利
return in triumph 凯旋而归
words.mnemonic: 罗马凯旋式→巨大胜利；triumph over 战胜

words.definition: vt. 逆转；n. 相反；背面；adj. 相反的

examples.en: The Supreme Court reversed the lower court's ruling by a majority.
examples.zh: 最高法院以多数票推翻了下级法院的裁决。

examples.en: The truck reversed out of the narrow alley with great care.
examples.zh: 卡车小心翼翼地倒出了狭窄的巷子。

words.usage: reverse a decision／trend 逆转决定、趋势；in reverse 反向；the reverse is true 反之亦然。派生：reversal n. 挫折；reversible adj. 可逆的。
collocations: reverse a decision 推翻决定
in reverse order 按相反顺序
reverse gear 倒车挡
words.mnemonic: re(回)+vers(转)→转回去→逆转；倒退

words.definition: n. 货币；流通；流行

examples.en: A weaker currency makes the country's exports more competitive.
examples.zh: 货币走弱使该国出口更具竞争力。

examples.en: The phrase quickly gained currency on social media platforms.
examples.zh: 这个说法迅速在社交媒体平台上流行开来。

words.usage: 熟词僻义：gain／lose currency 开始流行／不再流行；foreign currency 外币；currency devaluation 货币贬值。派生：current adj. 当前的。
collocations: foreign currency 外币
gain currency 开始流行
currency devaluation 货币贬值
words.mnemonic: cur(流)+rency→流通之物→货币；流行

words.definition: n. 监视；监控

examples.en: The suspect had been under close police surveillance for weeks.
examples.zh: 这名嫌疑人已受到警方数周的严密监视。

examples.en: Privacy groups oppose mass digital surveillance by governments.
examples.zh: 隐私组织反对政府实施大规模数字监控。

words.usage: under surveillance 受到监视；surveillance cameras 监控摄像头；mass／electronic surveillance 大规模、电子监控。源自法语，与 survey 同源。
collocations: under surveillance 受到监视
surveillance cameras 监控摄像头
electronic surveillance 电子监控
words.mnemonic: sur(上)+veill(看守)→在上面盯着→监视

words.definition: n. 追求；追逐；消遣

examples.en: The relentless pursuit of profit can come at the expense of ethics.
examples.zh: 对利润的一味追求可能以牺牲道德为代价。

examples.en: In pursuit of a quieter life, the couple moved to the countryside.
examples.zh: 为了追求更宁静的生活，这对夫妇搬到了乡下。

words.usage: in pursuit of 追求；in hot pursuit 穷追不舍；可数名词另指消遣（leisure pursuits）。动词 pursue a goal 追求目标。派生：pursuer n. 追赶者。

confusables.note: 劝说，u 后接 a 勿混

collocations: in pursuit of 追求
in hot pursuit 穷追不舍
leisure pursuits 业余消遣
words.mnemonic: pur(向前)+suit(跟随)→向前追→追求；消遣

words.definition: n. 过剩，盈余；adj. 过剩的，多余的

examples.en: The trade surplus widened as exports outpaced imports last year.
examples.zh: 去年出口增速超过进口，贸易顺差扩大。

examples.en: Surplus grain was sold abroad to stabilize domestic prices.
examples.zh: 过剩粮食被销往国外以稳定国内粮价。

words.usage: trade surplus 贸易顺差，反义 trade deficit 逆差；budget surplus 预算盈余；surplus grain 过剩粮食。词根 sur 超过＋plus 多，即多出来的部分。
collocations: trade surplus 贸易顺差
budget surplus 预算盈余
surplus value 剩余价值
words.mnemonic: sur(超)+plus(多)→多出来→盈余；过剩

words.definition: n. 奖，奖品；vt. 授予，判给

examples.en: She was awarded the Nobel Prize for her pioneering research.
examples.zh: 她因开创性研究被授予诺贝尔奖。

examples.en: The court awarded the victim substantial compensation for his injuries.
examples.zh: 法院判给受害者一大笔伤害赔偿金。

words.usage: award sb sth 或 award sth to sb 授予；be awarded 获颁；award 还可指法院判给的赔偿金。辨析：award 因成就授予，reward 酬谢报答，考研常考对比。
collocations: award a prize 授奖
win an award 获奖
award compensation 判给赔偿金
words.mnemonic: 与 reward 同尾：award 授奖，reward 回报

words.definition: vt. 使苏醒，使复兴；vi. 复苏

examples.en: Interest in traditional crafts has revived among young consumers.
examples.zh: 年轻消费者对传统手工艺的兴趣再度兴起。

examples.en: The government introduced stimulus measures to revive the sluggish economy.
examples.zh: 政府出台刺激措施以振兴疲软的经济。

words.usage: revive the economy 振兴经济；revive from fainting 苏醒。派生：revival n. 复兴，a revival of interest 兴趣回潮；同词根 viv 生命。
collocations: revive the economy 振兴经济
a revival of interest 兴趣回潮
revive old memories 唤起旧忆
words.mnemonic: re(再)+viv(生命)+e→再给生命→复苏

words.definition: adj. 累积的；渐增的

examples.en: The cumulative effect of sleep deprivation can be severe.
examples.zh: 睡眠不足的累积效应可能相当严重。

examples.en: Cumulative greenhouse gas emissions drive long-term climate change.
examples.zh: 温室气体的累积排放驱动着长期气候变化。

words.usage: cumulative effect／impact 累积效应，环境与医学文章高频；cumulative total 累计总数。派生：accumulate v. 积累；accumulation n. 积聚。

confusables.note: 有疗效的，ra 替代 mu

collocations: cumulative effect 累积效应
cumulative total 累计总数
cumulative damage 累积损伤
words.mnemonic: cumul(堆积，同 accumulate)+ive→越堆越多→累积

words.definition: adj. 看不见的；无形的

examples.en: Microplastics are virtually invisible to the naked eye.
examples.zh: 微塑料肉眼几乎看不见。

examples.en: Smith described competition as the invisible hand of the market.
examples.zh: 斯密将竞争描述为市场的「看不见的手」。

words.usage: invisible to sb／the naked eye 对某人、肉眼不可见；the invisible hand 看不见的手，经济学熟语；invisible exports 无形出口。
collocations: the invisible hand 看不见的手
invisible to the naked eye 肉眼看不见
invisible trade 无形贸易
words.mnemonic: in(不)+vis(看)+ible→看不见的

words.definition: adj. 奢侈的；过度的；夸大的

examples.en: Critics attacked the extravagant spending on the royal wedding.
examples.zh: 批评者抨击王室婚礼上的奢侈花费。

examples.en: His extravagant claims about the product were not backed by evidence.
examples.zh: 他对该产品夸大其词的说法并无证据支持。

words.usage: extravagant spending／lifestyle 奢侈花销、奢靡生活方式；extravagant claims 夸张说法。派生：extravagance n. 奢侈；近义 lavish 铺张。
collocations: extravagant spending 奢侈的开销
extravagant claims 夸大的说法
an extravagant lifestyle 奢靡的生活方式
words.mnemonic: extra(超)+vag(游荡)+ant→游荡出格→奢侈的

words.definition: vt. 压倒；使不知所措；制服

examples.en: She was overwhelmed by the sheer volume of emails after the holiday.
examples.zh: 假期过后，铺天盖地的邮件让她不知所措。

examples.en: The champions overwhelmed their opponents in the deciding set.
examples.zh: 卫冕冠军在决胜盘中完全压倒了对手。

words.usage: be overwhelmed by／with sth 被压垮、应接不暇；overwhelming majority 压倒性多数，考研高频。派生：overwhelming adj. 势不可挡的。
collocations: be overwhelmed by 被压垮
overwhelming majority 压倒性多数
an overwhelming urge 强烈的冲动
words.mnemonic: over(压过)+whelm(淹没)→整个盖住→压倒；不知所措
